description:
DONE s396c.  #314 family F-C part 1, the last reachable family of that task.

perl 5.36's n-at-a-time foreach.  PPI cannot lex it (it only knows
`foreach [my] $scalar (LIST) BLOCK`), so the compound statement keeps just
`for my` and the rest lands in a flat sibling — the same mis-lex as the
refaliasing foreach (#327), repaired the same way: rewrite the RAW TOKEN
STREAM, then reparse.  _repair_nary_foreach in Pl/Parser2.pm.

THE RE-SPELLING, all of it mechanisms PCL already had:

    for my ($q, $r) (@a) { BODY } continue { CONT }
      =>  my @L = map \$_, (@a);
          my @PD; push @L, \$PD[scalar @PD] while @L % 2;
          my $I = 0;
          while ($I < @L) { \my $q = $L[$I]; \my $r = $L[$I+1]; BODY }
          continue { CONT; $I += 2 }

THREE DECISIONS, each settled by a probe against perl 5.40.3, not by reasoning:

 1. `map \$_, LIST`, NOT `\(LIST)`.  map ALIASES $_ to each element, so `\$_`
    is a write-through ref to the ORIGINAL - probed for arrays, several arrays,
    a hash, literals and `reverse`, all six identical to perl.  `\(LIST)`
    distributes over the list's TERMS, so `\(@Q, @A)` is TWO ARRAY REFS (perl's
    own answer), which silently gave 2 iterations instead of 6.
 2. `while` + `continue`, NOT a C-style `for`.  perl allows a continue block on
    this loop (op/for-many.t uses one with redo and next) and a C-style for
    cannot carry one.  Putting the STEP in the continue block is what makes the
    three non-local exits land where perl puts them: `next` runs the continue
    block and the step, `redo` runs neither, `last` leaves.
 3. The PAD array gives the short final chunk its own writable slot per missing
    variable.  A single shared pad would make two loop variables the same
    variable.

RESULT: t/op/for-many.t TRANSPILE-FAIL (0 of 71) -> 63 ok / 8.  Of the 8:
  * 2 are "invalid perl must be rejected" rows (`for our (...)`, `for () ()`
    must be syntax errors) - CLAUDE.md principle 9, out of scope;
  * 6 are ONE missing perl fact, read-only SCALARS -> task #330.

TWO PRE-EXISTING BUGS the probes turned up, both fixed in the same commit
because the rewrite runs into them:
  * `\(%h)` gave ONE HASH ref where perl gives 2N SCALAR refs (one per key and
    per value, the value refs write-through).  _child_is_list_expr had an array
    arm and no hash arm, and p-refgen-list had no hash-table arm; it now
    delegates to %p-flatten-list, the same flattener list assignment uses, so
    the ORDER matches `%h` everywhere else and the value boxes arrive unwrapped.
  * that widening also changed `(%h) = LIST` from
    `(p-list-= (vector %h) …)` to `(p-hash-= %h …)` - the ONE corpus-diff hit,
    verified by running perl-tests/aassign.t (0 new fails).

Guard: 7 rows in Pl/t/refaliasing-01.t including the INVERSE (an ordinary
one-variable foreach must be untouched).
subject: n-at-a-time foreach `for my ($q,$r) (LIST)` (perl 5.36) - PPI cannot lex it (op/for-many.t 71 rows)
